adoption_basis: Pooled precision and recall improve, no query precision or recall declines, both earlier failure cases survive, and off/counted and no-profile behavior remain unchanged. Exact memory-ID retention is not guaranteed under capacity.

plan.candidate: With an explicit local reranker, collect the existing rerank_depth prefix of eligible symbol-linked memories before the four-note cap. Score question against reviewed-note title/body plus the selected code window supplying its validated link; use the existing blend order and then cap at four. No relevance threshold, hard exclusion, exact-symbol boost or diversity quota.
plan.rendering: Reviewed decision title and body first (256/3000 Unicode characters), linked symbol next, supplying selected code window last (2000 Unicode characters). Existing model truncation at 256 tokens applies.

onnx_runtime.note: Only the native universal2 library is used by Rust; no Python module import.

comparisons: Original local-inference-enabled build with the configured global reranker, off/counted/on.
Candidate with the same model, budgets, requests and global reranker, off/counted/on.
Historical model-free original, exact-priority and diversity receipts as secondary context; these are not isolated estimates of the late reranker effect.
acceptance: All calls and required tests pass; off/counted preserve packet content and memory membership across builds.
Both caller/callee pressure notes and all four direct compatibility contracts survive.
Improve links-on precision and lose no previously retrieved relevant memory versus the matched global-reranker baseline on each corpus.
Report gains/losses versus historical model-free original as well; do not claim a general improvement if it introduces new losses.
constraints: No thresholds, model switching, query/label edits or formatting tuning after observing results.
All fixtures are synthetic; no claim of independent held-out effectiveness.
Production sources remain unchanged until acceptance; preserve other workspace edits.

acceptance_qualification: The strict ID criterion fails only on shared-pressure/prose: six relevant notes compete for four slots; ledger is replaced by the equally relevant probe note, retaining 4/6 recall. Precision improves on the pressure set and is unchanged on the other sets. This is a qualified opt-in improvement, not full satisfaction of every literal frozen criterion.

latency_observation.scope: Observed local scoring time on tiny synthetic note batches, with the model already loaded by global reranking. Not a production latency claim; whole-call timings are confounded by concurrent compilation/evaluations.

final_boundary_correction: After primary measurements, code review found that source rerank_depth below four could reduce the linked-note allowance. Final collection uses max(4, rerank_depth). The primary depth is 32, so its ranking behavior is unchanged; the depth-one real-model CLI regression passed. No model, text rendering, labels, thresholds or ranking weights were tuned.
limitations: Synthetic memory-ID benchmark, not independently labelled real-session data or answer quality.
No rejection threshold: short candidate lists still include irrelevant notes.
Scores use a bounded prefix and the model truncates at 256 tokens; long-note and large-graph effectiveness remain unmeasured.
Only the blend mode and pinned MiniLM model were evaluated for quality.
No deployment, commit, push or default switch changes.
